mechanism_narrative: The sharp fall in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT implies fewer commuting-linked trips, which suppresses impulse and lunch-hour retail visits over the next four weeks. If mobility keeps shifting away from workplaces and transit, RETAIL_REC should remain below the prior four-week mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not recover from their current lows.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above 3 percentage points and stays elevated, people substitute home-based time for shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC down within one to two weeks. The effect should be visible even if other categories are stable.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within two weeks after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 3 points, or retail stays flat despite a further increase in residential time.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in PARKS together with falling TRANSIT indicates outdoor substitution rather than shopping-oriented travel. That mix should divert discretionary time away from retail and recreation, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stops declining over the next 28 days while PARKS remains elevated and TRANSIT remains depressed.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls by more than 5 points from one week to the next, that signals a new restriction shock that will quickly reduce retail visitation. The retail decline should appear within the next week and deepen over two to four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:transit is already far below baseline and still declining
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to drop in the week after a further transit decline, or transit falls without any corresponding retail weakening.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of weaker GROCERY_PHARM and stronger RESIDENTIAL indicates households are consolidating trips and staying home more often, which tends to cut casual retail outings. This should produce a lower RETAIL_REC average over the next four weeks than over the previous four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next month even though GROCERY_PHARM stays below baseline and RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: In a warm-weather leisure regime, elevated PARKS mobility acts as a substitute for shopping-center visits. When PARKS remains above 50 points for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC should weaken over the following two weeks as discretionary trips shift outdoors.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above 50 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Retail does not decline within two weeks after PARKS remains above 50 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both keep falling together, the loss of commuting traffic compounds and retail footfall declines faster than either series alone would imply. The retail effect should emerge within four weeks and be strongest when both measures move down simultaneously.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 28 days even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to decline together.

mechanism_narrative: Under reopening conditions, a rebound in GROCERY_PHARM followed by stabilization in WORKPLACES indicates normalization of out-of-home errands and weekday activity, which should lift retail visits. RETAIL_REC should rise over the next month only if both categories stop deteriorating and begin recovering.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its last-four-week average while GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES recover from current lows.
